title: Budgeted State Summaries for Communication-Efficient Multi-Agent Workflows
research_question: Can a workflow controller that adaptively compresses inter-agent messages into budgeted state summaries maintain task success while reducing communication cost and latency in multi-agent orchestration?
hypothesis: In multi-agent workflows, much coordination overhead comes from passing full reasoning traces when only a compact task-state summary is needed; an adaptive summarization layer that preserves decision-critical state will reduce token and latency costs with minimal or no drop in task success.
motivation: The knowledge base shows repeated rejected ideas around routing, replanning, escalation, and communication gating in agentic workflows, suggesting this area is active but overcrowded. A clearer gap is communication representation: the rejected ideas optimize when or which agent communicates, but not how workflow state should be compressed and handed off between agents. Separately, the self-adaptive systems literature emphasizes handling uncertainty in the analyze-plan loop and explicitly calls for extension to other domains and heterogeneous goals. This motivates transferring self-adaptive, uncertainty-aware control into multi-agent orchestration, but focusing on a less-saturated angle: adaptive message abstraction rather than yet another scheduler or router. If successful, this direction could improve throughput and cost efficiency for agentic systems without requiring new foundation models.
